ledger.claim: The rider's claim is narrow and specific: a $3.00 ERP charge for a gantry on a road the trip never used. The fare ledger itself concedes the point — the single ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at $3.00, is flagged on_optimal_route = false, and the optimal route's own ERP total is $0.00. The rider was billed for a gantry that is not on the route they booked.

The driver's own GPS trace never comes within 250 m of the charged gantry. The nearest fix to the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry is 330.73 m away, at 11:10:50, and the trace does not bracket the gantry's closest approach. Under POL-RD-09 a gantry is matched to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so the trace does not place the vehicle at this gantry.

This is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The $3.00 line should be refunded in full and the case recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The rider's claim does not depend on establishing a route deviation, and I do not overreach by asserting one. The trace measures 20.58 km against an optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%, which fails both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km). The derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The rider's remedy therefore rests on the ERP pass-through correction alone, not on POL-RD-02.

The driver's counter-statement — 'The ERP is charged by the system' — cites no evidence ID and identifies no gantry, road or route. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It does not discharge the driver's burden of showing the charge was properly incurred.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no external traffic cause can be tested or credited. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's bare assertion of a system charge, unsupported by any advisory, carries no weight, and the absence of an advisory is itself citable.

The fare ledger is internally consistent and unimpaired: it reconciles to a total charged of $30.55, with the $3.00 ERP line itemised separately. The refund sought is the $3.00 pass-through correction, which is below the $8.00 execution threshold and is a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), not a POL-RD-02 recomputation.

The rider's own claim is that an ERP charge of $3.00 was levied for a road the trip never used. The fare breakdown shows exactly one ERP line, the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry at $3.00, and the platform's own derived erp_gantry_proximity block records that this gantry is NOT on the optimal route (on_optimal_route = false) and that the closest the driver's trace ever came to it was 330.73 m, at fix index 128 (2026-08-30T11:10:50). Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The 330.73 m nearest approach exceeds the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 sets, so the gantry is unmatched and the $3.00 must be returned.

The distance-and-time side of the fare is not in dispute and should not be disturbed. The platform's own deviation computation on the trace records excess_km of 0.98 and excess_pct of 5.00 against the booked optimal of 19.6 km, and classifies the trip as 'no deviation'. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore fail: 5.00% is far below the 20% threshold and 0.98 km is only just above the 0.8 km absolute threshold, so the conjunctive test is not met. No distance or time refund is owed, and the driver keeps the metered fare he earned on a 20.58 km, 26.8 minute trip.

The driver's explanation for the ERP line - 'The ERP is charged by the system' - is not a defence to a billing-integrity correction. POL-RD-09(4) makes the refund available whether or not a deviation exists, and the driver's counterparty statement points to no artifact showing the vehicle crossed the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry. The trace shows the vehicle's nearest fix 330.73 m away, so the system charged a gantry the trip did not cross. The driver's assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 because it cites no evidence ID and no clause.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The rider disputed a $3.00 ERP charge for a road the trip never used. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02816) carries exactly one ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry', at $3.00, and the platform's own comparison of that gantry's coordinates (lat 1.289647, lng 103.863838) against the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02816) shows the closest the vehicle ever came was 330.73 m, at 11:10:50. POL-RD-09 treats a fix within 250 m of a gantry as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so the trace never passes this gantry. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, whether or not a deviation exists. The $3.00 is therefore returned to the rider, and the case is recorded for billing-integrity review. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND: it returns the contested ERP line only, not the whole fare.

The driver's answer — 'the ERP is charged by the system' — is no defence to this correction. It names no gantry, road or evidence, carries no weight, and cannot show the vehicle crossed a gantry the trace places 330.73 m away.

The distance and time charges are left standing. On the trace the driven distance is 20.58 km against the 19.6 km optimal route — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km; the percentage test fails, so no deviation is established, no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, and the driver keeps the metered distance and time charges for the 20.58 km, 26.8-minute trip.

No repeat-deviation or conduct finding arises. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) referral issues; the lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not used. The rider's profile likewise bars nothing and demands no extra corroboration (1 claim in 60 days, 0 substantiated). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 162 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown (TRP-02816), and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

Figures used: charged_total $30.55 (EV-FARE-02816); ERP line $3.00; optimal distance 19.6 km and trace distance 20.58 km (EV-GPS-02816); nearest fix 330.73 m. The ruling rests on the fare breakdown and the GPS trace, both at full weight 1.0. Its monetary effect, $3.00, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes on issue. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the $3.00 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' ERP line on trip TRP-02816 is unmatched by the GPS trace (nearest fix 330.73 m, outside the 250 m crossing radius) and is refunded as a standalone billing-integrity correction; record this as a billing-integrity finding.
